newsitem.title: TURKEY: Romania and Ukraine draw closer to treaty.
newsitem.headline: Romania and Ukraine draw closer to treaty.

text.p: The presidents of Romania and Ukraine held talks at a conference of Black Sea countries in Istanbul on Monday and drew closer to an agreement on a treaty important to Bucharest's chances for early NATO entry.
The treaty will confirm existing borders and enshrine rights for each country's ethnic minorities.
Romanian President Emil Constantinescu said after the meeting with Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma that they were moving towards an agreement over the treaty.
"The treaty is going to be finalised at the beginning of May," Constantinescu said after the meeting.
Romania won praise from the West for signing a treaty last year ending old rifts over borders and ethnic minorities with its western neighbour Hungary.

Western leaders say a similar treaty with Kiev would improve Romania's chances of being included in NATO along with Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic when the alliance holds its summit meeting in Madrid in July.

Romania's new leaders view Ukraine's territorial integrity as important for regional security. Clinching the treaty would also help Ukraine against claims by Russian nationalists to the Black Sea port of Sevastopol.
